# tfutils_aws_dynamodb_items_absent_wait (Resource)

Creates nothing. On destroy, waits until the table has no item whose string attribute `attribute_name` equals `attribute_value`, for example until external-dns removes the registry items it owns. Destroy fails with the keys of the remaining items when the delete timeout passes. Make the resources whose cleanup the controller does depend on this resource, and this resource depend on the controller.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tfutils_aws_dynamodb_items_absent_wait" "external_dns" {
  table_name      = "external-dns"
  attribute_name  = "o"
  attribute_value = var.cluster_name

  provider = tfutils.route53

  depends_on = [helm_release.external_dns]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `attribute_name` (String) Name of the string attribute to match.
- `attribute_value` (String) Value of the attribute that the items to wait for have.
- `table_name` (String) Name of the DynamoDB table.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<table_name>/<attribute_name>=<attribute_value>`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
